## Experiment

Repeats [`solo` at `medium` thinking](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium/summary.md) (`gemini-3.8-flash`, 500 steps, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, 50-pair `flash` subset) with compaction raised from 64K to 128K tokens, to decide which context window to standardize on. It ran on Vertex AI, while the 64K run used AI Studio; for `solo` the provider only changes waiting time, since there is no partner agent to fall out of sync with.

## Observations

- 37/50 (74%) at 128K vs. 33/50 at 64K. Pair by pair, 4 pairs passed only at 128K (`pallets_click_task/2068` (5,11), `pallets_click_task/2800` (1,3), `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8), `pallets_jinja_task/1559` (4,8)) and none only at 64K (exact two-sided test, p = 0.125). `pallets_click_task/2800` (1,3) had never been solved by `solo` before.
- The larger window cut compaction sharply: median 1 compaction per agent (5 at 64K), and 34 of 50 agents compacted at all (all 50 at 64K).
- Agents also finished sooner and cheaper: median 74 steps (133 at 64K), no agent at the 500-step limit (3 at 64K), and `$65.46` total vs. `$82.07`. Fewer compactions means fewer summarization calls and less re-reading of files after each summary.
- With 128K, `solo` (37/50) comes within one pair of `coop --git` at `medium` with 64K (38/50): 2 pairs passed only in `coop --git` and 1 only here. The matching `coop --git` run at 128K is in progress.
